qualification.details: Candidates having AOCP Trade Apprenticeship from Ordnance Factories, AOCP Trade Apprenticeship from a Govt./Private organization with Government affiliation, and other feeder trades as stated above from both Ordnance Factories and Govt./Private organizations having Govt. affiliation, and from Govt. ITI, shall be considered. | Priority order for consideration: | First priority: AOCP Trade Apprentices of Ordnance Factories, AOCP Trade Apprentices from Govt./Private organizations having Govt. affiliation, and candidates already engaged on Tenure Basis as CPW/DBW with a 3-month training certificate (1 month in-house on Safe Handling of explosives/ammunitions/safety norms + 2 months On-Job training) from MIL Group of Factories. Only if the required number of candidates is not available from these categories will candidates from the other feeder trades be considered for Trade Test. Candidates having NAC issued by NCVT in the AOCP trade & Feeder trades shall be considered for engagement on Tenure Basis; marks of the NAC mark sheet will be used for preparing the merit list. Candidates engaged from feeder trades other than AOCP (who don't possess the 3-month training certificate) will be given a compulsory 1-month in-house training followed by 2 months of On-Job training, after which a certificate acceptable across all MIL Group of Factories will be issued. Candidates belonging to feeder trades other than AOCP will also be engaged as Tenure Based CPW, subject to a consent/undertaking (Appendix-III) from the candidate.

salary_details.rate of pay: 1/30th of the basic pay of the relevant pay scale plus dearness allowance, for 8 hours of work a day
salary_details.dearness allowance: Central DA as prevalent will be applicable
salary_details.house rent allowance: As per classification of cities (when Company Quarter is not available); Company Quarters given priority where available, with license fee deducted as per rates applicable to regular Workmen
salary_details.annual increase: 3% (rounded to next ten rupees) on Basic Pay during tenure, subject to satisfactory performance
salary_details.other benefits: EPF, coverage under Employee's Compensation Act 1923, Bonus (if applicable) as per Bonus Act 1965, Night Duty Allowance (as applicable), Risk Allowance (as applicable), 30 days' leave per year (2.5 days credited per month), safety and protective gear, Maternity Benefits for female personnel as per the Maternity Benefit Act 1961
salary_details.details: Employment can be terminated at any time during the tenure by giving one month's notice by either party, or payment of the Basic Pay + DA components in lieu of notice. Tenure Based Personnel are NOT entitled to Promotions, OT Allowance, Loans/Advances/Interest Subsidies, Medical Facilities, Contingency Advance, School Fee Reimbursement, LTC/LTA Facilities, Study Leave, or Sponsorship for Higher Studies, and this engagement does not confer any right to claim the status of a regular employee.

selection_process: Selection is based on marks scored in the NAC (NCVT) mark sheet and Trade Test/Practical Test

in order of merit. HEF may decide the cut-off percentage for calling candidates for the Trade Test based on total marks secured in the NAC issued by NCVT. The merit list is prepared based on combined marks in the NAC (NCVT) mark sheet and Trade Test/Practical Test

with a weightage of 80% for NAC (NCVT) Exam and 20% for Trade Test/Practical Test. Order of preference while preparing the merit list: First preference: Ex-apprentices of AOCP trade trained in Ordnance Factories under MIL. Second preference: AOCP trade apprentices from DoO (C&S) other than MIL Group

and AOCP from Government/Private Organizations having Government affiliation. Third preference: Candidates engaged on Tenure Basis as CPW/DBW with the 3-month training certificate from MIL Group of Factories. Last preference: Trade apprentices of Ordnance Factories and Government/Private organizations having Government affiliation in the feeder stream trades. Candidates qualifying in the NAC (NCVT) and Trade Test/Practical Test will be called for Document Verification in order of merit

limited to the number of posts notified (discipline/category-wise). In case of rejection during Document Verification due to non-availability of required documents or not meeting the advertised criteria
additional candidates will be called in order of merit
limited to the number rejected. If a candidate in the merit list is found ineligible or fails to report within the stipulated period
a waitlisted candidate from the same category will be considered.
how_to_apply: Download and print the Application Form.
Fill up the application form in BLOCK LETTERS only.

Attach self-attested copies of required documents: proof of Date of Birth, Educational Qualification Certificate, NCVT (NAC) certificate and mark sheet in the specified trades, 3-month training certificate (if available), Experience Certificate, Caste Certificate (if applicable), and two self-attested passport-size photographs (one pasted on the form, one extra).

OBC candidates must also submit the declaration at Appendix-I; Ex-Servicemen candidates must submit the undertaking at Appendix-II; candidates from feeder trades other than AOCP must submit the consent/undertaking at Appendix-III.
Superscribe the envelope clearly as "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TENURE BASED CPW PERSONNEL ON CONTRACT BASIS."

Send the hard copy of the application, along with all enclosures, to: The Chief General Manager, High Explosives Factory, Khadki, Pune, Maharashtra, Pin-411003, so as to reach on or before the closing date.

content_sections.heading: HEF Khadki CPW Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: High Explosives Factory has announced a total of 85 vacancies for the post of Tenure Based CPW, with reservation for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, EWS, and other classes as per Government Reservation Rules.

content_sections.text: Candidates having AOCP Trade Apprenticeship from Ordnance Factories, AOCP Trade Apprenticeship from a Govt./Private organization with Government affiliation, and other feeder trades as stated above from both Ordnance Factories and Govt./Private organizations having Govt. affiliation, and from Govt. ITI, shall be considered. Priority order for consideration: First priority: AOCP Trade Apprentices of Ordnance Factories, AOCP Trade Apprentices from Govt./Private organizations having Govt. affiliation, and candidates already engaged on Tenure Basis as CPW/DBW with a 3-month training certificate (1 month in-house on Safe Handling of explosives/ammunitions/safety norms + 2 months On-Job training) from MIL Group of Factories. Only if the required number of candidates is not available from these categories will candidates from the other feeder trades be considered for Trade Test. Candidates having NAC issued by NCVT in the AOCP trade & Feeder trades shall be considered for engagement on Tenure Basis; marks of the NAC mark sheet will be used for preparing the merit list. Candidates engaged from feeder trades other than AOCP (who don't possess the 3-month training certificate) will be given a compulsory 1-month in-house training followed by 2 months of On-Job training, after which a certificate acceptable across all MIL Group of Factories will be issued. Candidates belonging to feeder trades other than AOCP will also be engaged as Tenure Based CPW, subject to a consent/undertaking (Appendix-III) from the candidate.

content_sections.heading: HEF Khadki CPW Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is based on marks scored in the NAC (NCVT) mark sheet and Trade Test/Practical Test, in order of merit. HEF may decide the cut-off percentage for calling candidates for the Trade Test based on total marks secured in the NAC issued by NCVT. The merit list is prepared based on combined marks in the NAC (NCVT) mark sheet and Trade Test/Practical Test, with a weightage of 80% for NAC (NCVT) Exam and 20% for Trade Test/Practical Test . Order of preference while preparing the merit list: First preference: Ex-apprentices of AOCP trade trained in Ordnance Factories under MIL. Second preference: AOCP trade apprentices from DoO (C&S) other than MIL Group, and AOCP from Government/Private Organizations having Government affiliation. Third preference: Candidates engaged on Tenure Basis as CPW/DBW with the 3-month training certificate from MIL Group of Factories. Last preference: Trade apprentices of Ordnance Factories and Government/Private organizations having Government affiliation in the feeder stream trades. Candidates qualifying in the NAC (NCVT) and Trade Test/Practical Test will be called for Document Verification in order of merit, limited to the number of posts notified (discipline/category-wise). In case of rejection during Document Verification due to non-availability of required documents or not meeting the advertised criteria, additional candidates will be called in order of merit, limited to the number rejected. If a candidate in the merit list is found ineligible or fails to report within the stipulated period, a waitlisted candidate from the same category will be considered.

OBC candidates must also submit the declaration at Appendix-I; Ex-Servicemen candidates must submit the undertaking at Appendix-II; candidates from feeder trades other than AOCP must submit the consent/undertaking at Appendix-III. faq.question: Q1. What is HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is High Explosives Factory, Khadki's engagement drive for 85 Tenure Based Chemical Process Worker (CPW) personnel on contract basis, for manufacturing and handling of explosives and hazardous chemicals.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 85 vacancies are available, distributed as UR-35, OBC-23, SC-13, ST-06, and EWS-08.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date to apply is 18 September 2026.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational/technical qualification for HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must hold a National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) issued by NCVT in the AOCP (Attendant Operator Chemical Plant) trade, or in specified feeder trades such as Fitter General, Electrician, Machinist, Turner, and others.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The maximum age for General category candidates is 40 years, with age relaxation of 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), and Military Service period + 3 years for Ex-Servicemen.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There is no application fee (Nil) for this recruitment.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply for HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must download and print the application form, fill it in Block Letters, attach the required self-attested documents, and send the hard copy by post to the Chief General Manager, High Explosives Factory, Khadki, Pune, before the closing date.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for HEF Khadki CPW Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Selection is based on a merit list combining NAC (NCVT) mark sheet marks (80% weightage) and Trade Test/Practical Test marks (20% weightage), followed by Document Verification.

faq.question: Q9. What is the pay for HEF Khadki CPW?
faq.answer: The Basic Pay is Rs. 19,900/- + DA, with additional benefits including HRA, EPF, Bonus (if applicable), and a 3% annual increase on Basic Pay subject to satisfactory performance.

faq.question: Q10. What is the tenure period for HEF Khadki CPW engagement?
faq.answer: The engagement is initially for one year from the date of engagement, extendable up to a maximum of four years, based on factory requirement and individual performance.
